newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oil tugs ready to help export Iraqi oil from Bakr.
newsitem.headline: Oil tugs ready to help export Iraqi oil from Bakr.

text.p: Iraq has placed two tug boats at its Mina al-Bakr oil export terminal in the northern Gulf to prepare for loading tankers under the United Nations oil-for-food deal, Gulf shipping sources said on Thursday.
But it was still unclear when crude exports from the Gulf terminal, 12 miles (19km) off the southern Fao Peninsula, would resume for the first time in six years.
"Both of the tugs are at al-Bakr...It is ready for operation," one shipping source in the region said.
A Turkish-flagged tanker is expected on Friday to begin loading the first Iraqi oil cargo from the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan, the Anatolian news agency reported on Thursday.
Al-Bakr is vital to Iraq's marketing efforts as it allows Baghdad to recapture market share from Gulf producers such as Iran and Kuwait in lucrative Asian markets.

Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed this week said that exports from Mina al-Bakr would begin Friday or Saturday but this has been delayed because of the need to install a new meter to monitor how much crude is exported.
No fixtures were reported in the shipping market to take a tanker to al-Bakr, Gulf shipping sources said.
U.N.-appointed overseers to the oil-for-food deal have so far approved only one sales ontract which was for Turkish state oil firm TUPRAS to lift 75,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Traders have anticipated that some 300,000 bpd of crude would be pumped through al-Bakr.
But Gulf shippers want more information on the structural tolerance of the terminal, its navigational systems and what draft restrictions SOMO is implementing at the port.
A functional test of the terminal can only be done once a tanker arrives at the port becuase it has no storage tanks.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) sent faxes earlier this year to potential customers that al-Bakr would be able to export Basrah Light and possibly Fao Blend.
U.S. Coastal Corp sought to fix an Ultra Large Crude Carrier (ULCC) to load crude at al-Bakr in September for its refinery in the Caribbean island of Aruba.
Iraq will export $2 billion of its oil from Ceyhan and al-Bakr over the next six months on a renewable basis.
